entries.test: Representative surveys available by publication showing how many people had tried generative AI and whether users reported dissatisfaction would test this claim.
entries.note: “Practically everyone” asserts near-universal trial; an executive-only survey cannot establish that population-wide claim.

entries.test: The CNBC poll's trial rate and sampling population, together with representative AI adoption surveys, would establish whether the cited evidence contradicts widespread nonuse of AI.
entries.note: The proposition captures the factual inference rather than the accompanying praise. Generalizing from surveyed executives to people broadly requires scrutiny.

entries.test: The October 2024 CNBC Technology Executive Council poll's published results would show whether 25% of respondents considered Microsoft Copilot worth its cost.
entries.note: This reports the frequency of respondents' judgments, which is a factual claim.

entries.test: Representative surveys of generative AI awareness, trial, and reported reasons for delaying adoption would show whether people were broadly evaluating its usefulness rather than ignoring it.
entries.note: This describes a current public attitude, not a forecast that generative AI will work.
